title.narrative: Oc2.Ind1. Strategic litigation undertaken towards realisation of tribal rights in the 8 states

description.narrative: Oc2.Ind1. Strategic litigation undertaken towards realisation of tribal rights in the 8 states

comment.narrative: Lawyers CSOs and community leaders lacking the necessary tools and skills to assist Adivasi in their quest for justice compensation and better empowerment of the communities to engage with issues of human rights law and especially IP rights. The lack of research documentation and monitoring of human rights abuses suffered by Adivasi in these regions as a consequence of mining industry practices such as land acquisition denial of access to natural resources and subsequent working conditions. This lack of data reports and media coverage are direct cause of why these corporation abuses which also are violation of human rights are not known by the large public in India but also around the world.

At least 30 pieces of evidence of land rights abuses work conditions and degradation of the environment affecting indigenous peoples are collected by scoping mission legal clinics and the database. At least 10 are used to inform litigation judgment implementation advocacy efforts.No. of judgements in favour of tribal rights at local national regional levels No. of victims of extractive industries benefiting from legal assistance and interventions No. of extractive companies introducing accountable policies and practices in line with tribal rights Strategic Legal support provided in at least 8 cases 1 x state

Final target to be achieved by Y5.2 One favorable judgement at the federal level in Y1.3 122 beneficiaries received direct support from legal clinics in Y1. comment.narrative: Lawyers CSOs and community leaders lacking the necessary tools and skills to assist Adivasi in their quest for justice compensation and better empowerment of the communities to engage with issues of human rights law and especially IP rights. The lack of research documentation and monitoring of human rights abuses suffered by Adivasi in these regions as a consequence of mining industry practices such as land acquisition denial of access to natural resources and subsequent working conditions. This lack of data reports and media coverage are direct cause of why these corporation abuses which also are violation of human rights are not known by the large public in India but also around the world.

At least 30 pieces of evidence of land rights abuses work conditions and degradation of the environment affecting indigenous peoples are collected by scoping mission legal clinics and the database. At least 10 are used to inform litigation judgment implementation advocacy efforts.No. of judgements in favour of tribal rights at local national regional levels No. of victims of extractive industries benefiting from legal assistance and interventions No. of extractive companies introducing accountable policies and practices in line with tribal rights Strategic Legal support provided in at least 8 cases 1 x state
